searchText: Are there any downsides to allowing exited validators to rejoin the network as active validators again ? the main thing is that it complicates the protocol to have to recycle validator indices we use the validator index as a stand-in for the validator identity in several places and it ends up being cleaner/simpler to have a "one-way" lifecycle graph <@415109946682769408> has a talk on this you would end up adding loops to the lifecycle graph which just makes things more complex simple enough to just re-join as a new validator if that is what you wished to do but their indexes would stay the same no ? the only thing that changes would be the current validator status. But then their old balance will be stuck in the beacon chain doing nothing in that case afaiui there is some intention to allow more flexibility here in later phases right so the fields in the state tracking who is where in the lifecycle would need to be managed by more complex code we can start (esp in early phases) with the simple "naive" thing >simple enough to just re-join as a new validator if that is what you wished to do With the caveat that doing so requires depositing at least 1 more ETH. But this could be fixed with a kind of modified transfer along the lines of `transfer_into_new_validator` I guess that could be something we can do for now in the time being. We did get some questions on if there was any way to 'pause' your stake and resume it later if you choose to <@550420431744794624> you are pointing out that there is a "sub 1-ETH" territory where this isn't as simple as we would want? <@476250636548308992> yeah the "pause" thing is something i hear about a lot as well... there are a bunch of trade-offs here to consider around validator experience, protocol complexity and according to some regulatory uncertainty if it becomes clear we need to do something different to make an attractive validator experience then im confident we can sort it out I have found that lot of the "pause" questions are from people thinking they will be slashed for going offline. yeah there is a fair bit of misconceptions on it, but also it does help them feel safer and have a larger degree of control over their staking activity > <@550420431744794624> you are pointing out that there is a "sub 1-ETH" territory where this isn't as simple as we would want? Not sure I follow. All I am trying to point out is that if you exit and want to start up again. The way to do it is to transfer to a new validator (index). To do so requires a validator to exist at this index which can only be the case if there was a previous deposit. This requires a minimum of 1 eth sent to the deposit contract. They might not want to continously online for a long period of time, because managing your validator does require some amount of effort consistently gotcha i was even thinking phase 0 pre-transfer There are no transfers in phase 0, though. And would it not be simpler to just allow a validator to move from exited to active (assuming it has enough in terms of funds, of course) It does mess with the issuance of indicies tho. The root in the deposit contract would also get out of sync Also does anyone have a link to <@415109946682769408> talk on validator lifecycles ? Seems like something quite relevant to this yeah i suppose that is the strongest argument to keep the (phase 0) status quo -- the deposit contract would have to change and there has been a lot of formal verification effort put into it so far <@476250636548308992> she has given a few versions of the talk at various confernces -- edcon 2019 and devcon (this year i think) this was easier to find than i expected 🙂 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P4loHGCplX4 Or eth2 would have to maintain the root differently. (Possibly with 2 roots) Thanks ! <@539495253418180618> multi-level validator indices! welcome >multi-level validator indices! The fun begins! Woot! deposit index doesn't necessarily have to match validator index. I don't think the contract needs to change at all. Maybe client implementer tooling that makes the assumption. another thing to keep in mind when thinking about "validator index resuse" is how things differ across forks and how message interpretation across fork boundaries could be complicated by this that's fair, we are indexing by pubkey there If the validator lifecycle changed the EXITED state to INACTIVE and allowed movement back to ACTIVE it's not really reusing an index, though Also note that we already support topups with deposits. Deposit index is bound to get out of sync with validator index on the first top up. <@476250636548308992> <@539495253418180618> thanks! there is also a spec v0.8.3 version (from p.45) at devcon: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1MZ-E6TVwomt4rqz-P2Bd_X3DFUW9fWDQkxUP_QJhkyw/edit?pli=1#slide=id.g621e1673fb_21_195 great, thanks for this ! Will dig into it <@144468805697929216> a specific scenario is escaping me but i believe there are some assumptions around slashing to the effect that validators move *once* through this lifecycle and that it is unidirectional Perhaps transfers need to come back in phase 0 then? At current the idea of an "attractive validator experience" is a long way from the reality of validating. i think its still up for debate

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: Are there any downsides to allowing exited validators to rejoin the network as active validators again ?

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: the main thing is that it complicates the protocol to have to recycle validator indices

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: we use the validator index as a stand-in for the validator identity in several places

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: and it ends up being cleaner/simpler to have a "one-way" lifecycle graph

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: <@415109946682769408> has a talk on this

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: you would end up adding loops to the lifecycle graph which just makes things more complex

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: simple enough to just re-join as a new validator if that is what you wished to do

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content:
but their indexes would stay the same no ? the only thing that changes would be 
the current validator status.

But then their old balance will be stuck in the beacon chain doing nothing in that case

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: afaiui there is some intention to allow more flexibility here in later phases

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: right so the fields in the state tracking who is where in the lifecycle would need to be managed by more complex code

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: we can start (esp in early phases) with the simple "naive" thing

excerpts.author: carlbeek
excerpts.content:
>simple enough to just re-join as a new validator if that is what you wished to do

With the caveat that doing so requires depositing at least 1 more ETH. But this could be fixed with a kind of modified transfer along the lines of `transfer_into_new_validator`

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: I guess that could be something we can do for now in the time being. We did get some questions  on if there was any way to 'pause' your stake and resume it later if you choose to

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: <@550420431744794624> you are pointing out that there is a "sub 1-ETH" territory where this isn't as simple as we would want?

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: <@476250636548308992> yeah the "pause" thing is something i hear about a lot as well... there are a bunch of trade-offs here to consider around validator experience, protocol complexity and according to some regulatory uncertainty

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: if it becomes clear we need to do something different to make an attractive validator experience then im confident we can sort it out

excerpts.author: carlbeek
excerpts.content: I have found that lot of the "pause" questions are from people thinking they will be slashed for going offline.

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content:
yeah there is a fair bit of misconceptions on it, but also it does help them feel safer and 
have a larger degree of control over their staking activity

excerpts.author: carlbeek
excerpts.content:
> <@550420431744794624> you are pointing out that there is a "sub 1-ETH" territory where this isn't as simple as we would want?

Not sure I follow. All I am trying to point out is that if you exit and want to start up again. The way to do it is to transfer to a new validator (index). To do so requires a validator to exist at this index which can only be the case if there was a previous deposit. This requires a minimum of 1 eth sent to the deposit contract.

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content:
They might not want to continously online for a long period of time, because managing your validator 
does require some amount of effort consistently

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: gotcha

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: i was even thinking phase 0 pre-transfer

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: There are no transfers in phase 0, though.  And would it not be simpler to just allow a validator to move from exited to active (assuming it has enough in terms of funds, of course)

excerpts.author: carlbeek
excerpts.content: It does mess with the issuance of indicies tho. The root in the deposit contract would also get out of sync

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content: Also does anyone have a link to <@415109946682769408> talk on validator lifecycles ? Seems like something quite relevant to this

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: yeah i suppose that is the strongest argument to keep the (phase 0) status quo -- the deposit contract would have to change and there has been a lot of formal verification effort put into it so far

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: <@476250636548308992> she has given a few versions of the talk at various confernces -- edcon 2019 and devcon (this year i think)

excerpts.author: carlbeek

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: multi-level validator indices!

excerpts.author: ralexstokes

excerpts.author: carlbeek
excerpts.content:

The fun begins! Woot!

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: deposit index doesn't necessarily have to match validator index. I don't think the contract needs to change at all. Maybe client implementer tooling that makes the assumption.

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: another thing to keep in mind when thinking about "validator index resuse" is how things differ across forks and how message interpretation across fork boundaries could be complicated by this

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: that's fair, we are indexing by pubkey there

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: If the validator lifecycle changed the EXITED state to INACTIVE and allowed movement back to ACTIVE it's not really reusing an index, though

excerpts.author: protolambda
excerpts.content: Also note that we already support topups with deposits. Deposit index is bound to get out of sync with validator index on the first top up.
